title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Joint Emergency Response in Ukraine (JERU – Concern and Welthungerhilfe working in partnership) transferred cash to war-affected individuals to cover their basic needs for a three months period. The project reached 596 highly vulnerable individuals and successfully delivered Rapid Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance to people affected by shelling, forced displacement, and loss of habitable housing.. Marker 1.5 was selected because the primary objective was to provide emergency lifesaving assistant to war-affected individuals to cover their basic needs in times of crisis. The intervention strengthened household capacity to manage sudden economic shocks and contributed to the preservation of dignity and basic living standards.
